Hi again!

I'm still working on lavaan survey, using this (big) model, but now the main problem is the memory limits. Exploring the functions inside the lavaan.survey(), we detected that there're some matrix operations that are heavy and compromise the function efficiency. Below, follow the lines inside the code that are making everything worst. Does 
anyone know some tips that we can run this more efficient or not exceeding the memory size?




45. sample.cov.g <- as.matrix(svyvar(ov.formula, design=survey.design.g, na.rm=TRUE))
...
49. Gamma.cov.g <- Dplus %*% Gamma.cov.g %*% t(Dplus)
...
57 Gamma.g <- lavaan::lav_matrix_bdiag(Gamma.mean.g, Gamma.cov.g)

Source: https://github.com/cran/lavaan.survey/blob/master/R/lavaan.survey.R


Thanks,
Cheers!

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Lavaan Survey function in SEM and CFA is very slow...
parts:
> are heavy and compromise the function efficiency. Below, follow the
> lines inside the code that are making everything worst. Does
> anyone know some tips that we can run this more efficient or not
> exceeding the memory size?

> 49. Gamma.cov.g<-Dplus%*%Gamma.cov.g%*%t(Dplus)

Maybe you can adapt lavaan's lav_matrix_duplication_ginv_pre_post()
function, which usually expects a S %x% S matrix as the argument (and
therefore insists that the number of rows/cols is some number (n =
nrow(S)) squared. The current code is:

# pre AND post-multiply with D^+: D^+ %*% A %*% t(D^+)
# for square matrices only, with ncol = nrow = n^2
lav_matrix_duplication_ginv_pre_post <- function(A = matrix(0,0,0)) {

A <- as.matrix(A)

# number of columns
n2 <- NCOL(A)

# square A only, n2 = n^2
stopifnot(NROW(A) == n2, sqrt(n2) == round(sqrt(n2)))

# dimension
n <- sqrt(n2)

idx1 <- lav_matrix_vech_idx(n); idx2 <- lav_matrix_vechru_idx(n)
OUT <- (A[idx1,,drop=FALSE] + A[idx2,,drop=FALSE]) / 2
OUT <- (OUT[,idx1,drop=FALSE] + OUT[,idx2,drop=FALSE]) / 2
OUT
}

This would avoid creating the Dplus matrix, which can be huge (and is
very sparse).

Another option is to use the Matrix package, and define Dplus as a
sparse matrix.

Yves.
